head: claude/mi95-manager-scope-guard
title: MI-95: the manager session only manages — a check that names the commit, not another paragraph
body:
## MI-95 — the manager/worker division as a mechanism that bites

**The prose already existed. That is the point.** `CLAUDE.md` has carried the operator's rule verbatim since 2026-09-01. The 2026-09-03 day manager read that line at session start and was caught doing items the same morning. So this ships **a check, not a paragraph** — `scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py` fails a PR carrying a manager commit that touches a worker path, and names the commit and the path.

---

## ⚠️ Which of the manager's 2026-09-03 actions this would have BLOCKED, and which PERMITTED

**Population:** all 24 commits across all refs carrying `session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd`'s `Claude-Session:` trailer, graded by the shipped guard.

**Result: 0 of 24 fail R2. One fails R6.** That is the honest answer and it is not the flattering one.

| The action (from the dispatch) | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Hand-resolved 4 register merge conflicts (`OPEN-ITEMS.json`, `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json`, `SESSIONS.json`, `health-review-backlog.json`) | **PERMITTED** | All four are the manager's own registers. Resolving a conflict in your own instruments is management, and blocking it would stop the manager keeping the state of record. |
| Resolved the merge conflict on **#10893** | **PERMITTED** | Verified, not assumed: `e7738ac7` carries the manager's trailer and touches `.github/pr-landing/…`, `OPEN-ITEMS.json`, `MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json`, one work object. Every path in-surface. |
| Fixed the `artifact-validity-guard` / `claim-basis-guard` failures | **PERMITTED** | Measured: this landed as `e178d5d0` *"fix the backlog row my own guards rejected"*, touching only `health-review-backlog.json`. It was a **row** fix, not a **guard** fix. Had it touched `scripts/ci/`, it would have failed as `guard/CI logic`. |
| Authored 4 backlog rows with full resolution criteria | **PERMITTED — deliberately, and this is the contested call.** | See below. |
| Diagnosed the ClaudeBot defect by reading `claude_decision_bot.py` + the systemd journal | **NOT CAUGHT** | Reading source produces no commit. A commit-scoped check is structurally blind to it. Stated, not papered over. |
| Two turns ended with a sub-session blocked for 46 minutes | **NOT CAUGHT by R2; R6 fires once nearby** | R6 fails `f550f833` (the lease claim) — `SESSIONS.json` was **479 minutes** stale when the manager claimed the lease. That is the supervision-record signal, not the 46-minute one, which is live session state CI cannot read. |
| Merging PRs; recording operator decisions | **PERMITTED, by design** | A merge is not a commit this guard grades. Decisions land in `docs/claude/work/**`, in-surface. Both are named in the module docstring so a later reader does not "tighten" the surface into breaking them. |

### And where it does bite: the 2026-09-02 manager

**Population:** commits on `origin/main` since 2026-09-01 carrying each lease-holder's trailer.

| Session | Clean | **Would FAIL** |
|---|---|---|
| `session_011JWFxu…` (09-02 day manager) | 75 | **31** |
| `session_01AYPxs3…` (night manager) | 2 | 0 |
| `session_01Nopk1H…` (09-03 day manager) | 5 | 0 |

The 31 break down as: 36 unrecognised paths, 33 test authoring, 23 ops tooling, 23 application source, 23 guard/CI logic, 22 CI workflow logic, 9 `CLAUDE.md` prose, 3 deployment units. Top offenders: `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` (9), `CLAUDE.md` (9), `src/web/api/routers/diag.py` (4), `src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py` (3). **That is a manager building software, at scale, for a day** — and it is what this guard is for.

**Read the two tables together.** The guard bites hard where the building actually happened and barely touches yesterday's morning. If the operator's judgement is that 2026-09-03 *was* a bad day for supervision, then **R2 is not the rule that captures it** — the item-work was reading, reviewing and filing, none of which a commit-scoped guard sees. That is the honest limit, and it is why R6 exists rather than being left as a nice-to-have.

---

## Who counts as the manager — DERIVED, never declared

Both obvious implementations were **measured and rejected**:

- **Branch name.** Population: 18 of 252 remote branches with a merge-base against `main` match `manager|workflow-overhaul`. `claude/risk-manager-backstop` is a **worker** branch (`src/runtime/order_monitor.py`, `src/units/accounts/risk.py`) that matches; `claude/openprs-prune-merged-rows` carries no manager token and its first commit is `lease: heartbeat (manager sweep 08:12Z)`. The name is not the role.
- **Writing the manager's registers.** 30 of 252 branches write one. But 8 are `automation/reconcile-open-prs-*` bots, and `mi94-register-id-uniqueness` / `openprs-settled-reconciler` / `subsession-registry-coupling-handoff-check` are **worker** sessions whose subject matter *is* the registry. `OPEN-PRS.json` and `SESSIONS.json` are not manager-exclusive.

What identifies the manager is what **makes** it the manager: **it holds the lease.** `MANAGER-LEASE.json`'s git history is the roster — **3 sessions across 59 revisions** — joined to each commit's `Claude-Session:` trailer.

**It grades COMMITS, not the branch's net diff.** The acts that hurt most — resolving conflicts on *other* sessions' PRs — never appear in the manager's own PR. A branch-diff check would be blind to exactly the failure it exists for. On a merge it grades the **combined diff** (`git show -c`), so hand-resolved paths are seen and swept-along files are not.

---

## The contested call: filing a backlog row is PERMITTED, with no cap

Decided, not defaulted, and argued in full in the module docstring.

- **For:** "if you see something, say something" *requires* the manager to file what it notices, and a backlog row is the artifact that **routes work to a session**. Filing is the act of *not* taking the item.
- **Against, and it is not nothing:** four rows with full resolution criteria is real authoring effort — hours not spent supervising.
- **Why permissive wins:** the cost complained about is **attention**, and a path allowlist does not measure attention. A row cap would mostly catch diligent filing while missing a manager that spent the same hours reading source. **R6 is where attention actually gets graded.**
- **What would change it:** evidence that backlog volume correlates with R6 gaps. Measurable, but n=3 manager sessions — filed rather than guessed.

`CLAUDE.md` is the other judgement call: graded **by hunk, not by path**. Re-rendering the `SESSION-BRIEF` block passes; rewriting the canon does not.

---

## R6 — the positive duty, and only because it can be measured honestly

A commit advancing the lease heartbeat while `SESSIONS.json` is staler than the lease's own `ttl_minutes` fails. **The threshold is read from the file, not invented.**

**Population: 50 lease revisions with `state == held` and both timestamps readable** — median gap 18 min, p75 37, p90 66, max 480. At the 30-min heartbeat target it would fail **14 of 50** and get deleted rather than fixed; at the TTL it fails **2 of 50**.

⚠️ **It measures the RECORD of supervision, never supervision itself.** A manager who unblocked three sessions over Telegram and wrote nothing down grades stale — deliberate, because a cold successor can only pick up what the file names. It must never be cited as evidence that help was given. The live half is `scripts/ops/manager_view.py` (MI-89).

⚠️ A lease **claim** is graded too, and that is a decision with a real objection (an incoming manager inherits the outgoing one's staleness). Argued in the docstring; it is the single R6 fire on the 09-03 manager.

---

## The escape hatch is visible and argued, never a flag

`docs/claude/work/manager-scope-exception.yaml`, on the `spawn-priority-exception.yaml` pattern. **A live incident is not "an item."** Every field is VERIFIED: `pending` refuses, an expired entry refuses, a one-word `reason` refuses, and `paths` is scoped. **No bypass flag and no environment variable** — the cheapest way past this guard must be to route the work to a session.

## Proving the teeth

`--self-test` builds real git repos and plants each defect. **13 cases: 7 plants, 6 positive controls.** The controls matter as much as the plants — this guard *refuses a manager's work*, so an over-broad version would block the manager from managing, the opposite of what was asked.

Plants: manager commits `src/` · manager edits `CLAUDE.md` prose · manager resolves a `src/` conflict **on a worker's branch** · heartbeat with a registry staler than TTL · `pending` / expired / one-word-reason exceptions · untrailered commits → `unattributed`, never "compliant".
Controls: the identical diff from a **worker** session · manager on its own registers (backlog row included) · a `SESSION-BRIEF` re-render · a heartbeat with a fresh registry · a complete exception actually granting what it names.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **84 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP**, *"All relevant guards passed."* (An earlier run was 82/2; both failures were real and are fixed below.) `check_selftest_wiring.py` verifies the new self-test's wiring end-to-end.
- ⚠️ **`pytest`, `import-linter` and `ruff` were ABSENT** and 4 guards were failing on that alone. Installed and re-run rather than reported green — MI-94's mistake, not repeated.
- **`artifact-validity-guard` caught a real defect of mine**: both files cited `BL-20260903-MANAGER-CHECKLIST-GOES-STALE-SILENTLY`, which resolves to nothing (the row is `…-AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT`); one was truncated by comment wrapping. Fixed.
- **`pr-landing-guard` refused an earlier `changes_landing_machinery` declaration** — correctly: `run_guards.py` is not on its `LANDING_MACHINERY` list. That omission is filed as `BL-20260903-RUN-GUARDS-PY-IS-LANDING-MACHINERY-AND-CHECK-PR-LANDING-DOES-NOT-KNOW-IT` rather than fixed here, because widening that list hands the excuse to every guard PR and is out of MI-95's scope to decide.

## Landing

`"landing": "hold"`. ⚠️ **The token is imperfect and is disclosed as such**: `operator_asked_to_hold` names the *manager's* dispatch instruction, not the operator's, and the closed vocabulary has no token for "a manager asked". R12's condition was **checked, not assumed**, and is not met. Held because the dispatch says the blocked/permitted list above "is the honest test of whether the line is drawn in the right place" — a guard whose line placement has been submitted for review should not merge itself ahead of that review.

## Scope

Only the manager-scope definition, its guard, its exception file, and the `CLAUDE.md` paragraph pointing the existing rule at it. No order path, no strategy config, no risk caps, no live-VM runtime file. One finding filed rather than fixed.
